'''Dame Alison Mary Etheridge''' (born 1964)<ref name=whoswho/> is Professor of [[Probability]] and former Head of the Department of Statistics,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/all-people/alison-etheridge/|title=Alison Etheridge, Department of Statistics, University of Oxford|last=|first=|date=|website=Department of Statistics|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180716030607/http://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/all-people/alison-etheridge/|archive-date=16 July 2018|access-date=}}</ref> University of Oxford.<ref name=scopus>{{Scopus id}}</ref><ref name="Barton2004">{{cite journal|last1=Barton|first1=N. H.|last2=Etheridge|first2=A.M.|title=The Effect of Selection on Genealogies|journal=Genetics|volume=166|issue=2|year=2004|pages=1115–1131|issn=0016-6731|doi=10.1534/genetics.166.2.1115|pmid=15020491|pmc=1470728}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal

==Education==
Etheridge was educated at [[Smestow Academy|Smestow School]].<ref name=whoswho/> She read mathematics in [[New College, Oxford]], earning a bachelor's degree in 1985 and staying on for a year of master's research. After a traveling to [[McGill University]] from 1986 to 1987, with the support of the [[Canadian Rhodes Scholars Foundation]], she returned to Oxford as Sir Christopher Cox Junior Fellow and Tutor for Women in New College.<ref name=magd/> She completed a doctorate ([[DPhil]]) in 1989<ref name=etheridgephd/> for research supervised by David Albert Edwards.<ref name=mathgene/><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1016/0022-3115(85)90372-1| title = Instability of the rate equations for creep coupled to swelling| journal = Journal of Nuclear Materials| volume = 132| issue = 3| pages = 277–283| year = 1985| last1 = Etheridge | first1 = A. M. | last2 = Finnis | first2 = M. W. | bibcode = 1985JNuM..132..277E}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Following her PhD, Etheridge held research fellowships in Oxford and Cambridge and positions at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], The [[University of Edinburgh]], and [[Queen Mary University of London]] before returning to Oxford in 1997.<ref name=frs/>

Over the course of her career, her interests have ranged from abstract mathematical problems to concrete applications as reflected in her four books which range from a research monograph on mathematical objects called [[Superprocess|superprocesses]] to an exploration (co-authored with [[Mark H. A. Davis]]) of the percolation of ideas from the groundbreaking thesis of [[Louis Bachelier]] in 1900 to modern mathematical finance.<ref name=frs/>

Much of her recent research is concerned with mathematical models of population genetics, where she has been particularly involved in efforts to understand the effects of spatial structure of populations on their patterns of genetic variation.<ref name=frs/>

Etheridge has made significant contributions in the theory and applications of probability and in the links between them.<ref name=frs/> Her particular areas of research have been in measure-valued processes (especially [[superprocess]]es and their generalisations); in theoretical [[population genetics]]; and in [[mathematical ecology]].<ref name=frs/> A recent focus has been on the genetics of spatially extended populations, where she has exploited and developed inextricable links with infinite-dimensional [[stochastic]] analysis.<ref name=frs/> Her resolution of the so-called '[[torus|pain in the torus]]' is typical of her work in that it draws on ideas from diverse areas, from measure-valued processes to image analysis.<ref name=frs/> The result is a flexible framework for modelling biological populations which, for the first time, combines ecology and [[genetics]] in a tractable way, while introducing a novel and mathematically interesting class of [[stochastic process]]es.<ref name=frs/> The breadth of her contributions is further illustrated by the topics of her four books, which range from the history of [[Mathematical finance|financial mathematics]] to mathematical modelling in population genetics.<ref name=frs/><ref name=royal>{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/fellowship/2015/alison-etheridge/ |title = Professor Alison Etheridge FRS |publisher=The Royal Society |archivedate=2015-05-02 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150502203524/https://royalsociety.org/people/fellowship/2015/alison-etheridge/ |location=London}}</ref>

She was head of the University of Oxford's Department of Statistics, in a three-year post that ran until August 2022.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=14 November 2019 |title=Notices |url=https://gazette.web.ox.ac.uk/sites/default/files/gazette/documents/media/14_november_2019_-_no_5257_redacted.pdf |journal=University of Oxford Gazette |volume=150 |issue=5257 |pages=116–117}}</ref> She chairs the Mathematical Sciences sub-panel of the 2021 [[Research Excellence Framework]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 April 2021 |title=Main panel B full membership list |url=https://www.ref.ac.uk/media/1760/main-panel-b-full-membership-list-apr-2021.pdf |access-date=2022-03-14 |website=Research Excellence Framework}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Etheridge was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2015|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2015]].<ref name=frs/> and a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 2016. Her citation reads:
{{centred pull quote|for outstanding research on measure-valued stochastic processes and applications to population biology; and for international leadership and impressive service to the profession.<ref name=imsfellow>{{cite web |url=http://imstat.org/news/2016/06/22/1466613820072.html |title = IMS Fellows 2016 |publisher=Institute of Mathematical Statistics |archivedate=2017-01-10 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170110213250/http://imstat.org/news/2016/06/22/1466613820072.html}}</ref>}}
In 2017, she was elected as president of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics for a one-year term.<ref name=imsprez>{{cite web |url=http://imstat.org/officials/current_officials.html|title=Current officials|publisher=Institute of Mathematical Statistics |archivedate=2016-10-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161031192628/http://www.imstat.org/officials/current_officials.html}}</ref> She was awarded the [[Senior Anne Bennett Prize]] by the [[London Mathematical Society]] in 2017,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://aperiodical.com/2017/07/2017-lms-prize-winners-announced/|title= 2017 LMS prize winners announced|publisher=The Aperiodical|website=aperiodical.com|date= 16 July 2017}} Retrieved 2017-07-17</ref>
and was appointed [[Officer of the Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in the [[2017 Birthday Honours]] for services to science.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=61962|supp=y|page=B11|date=17 June 2017}}</ref> The University of Edinburgh awarded her an honorary [[Doctor of Science]] degree in 2018/19.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Honorary graduates 2018/19 |url=https://www.ed.ac.uk/about/people/honorary-degrees/2018-19 |access-date=2022-03-14 |website=The University of Edinburgh |date=12 December 2018 |language=en}}</ref> She has served on the [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] (EPSRC)'s Strategic Advisory Network and its Mathematical Sciences Strategic Advisory Team. She was appointed to the Council of the EPSRC in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 March 2018 |title=Prominent statistician appointed to the board of EPSRC |url=https://rss.org.uk/news-publication/news-publications/2018/general-news/prominent-statistician-appointed-to-the-board-of-e/ |access-date=2022-03-14 |website=rss.org.uk |publisher=Royal Statistical Society}}</ref>

She is a Trustee of the Royal Society and a member of its governing council.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 December 2019 |title=Committees, Working Groups, and Councils |url=https://royalsociety.org/sitecore/content/royal-society/configuration/Components/Api2/CommitteeDetailPage/ |access-date=2022-03-21 |website=royalsociety.org}}</ref> In September 2021 she became the chair of the [[Council for the Mathematical Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 June 2021 |title=Appointment of new CMS Chair |url=https://www.cms.ac.uk/wp/2021/06/09/appointment-of-new-cms-chair/ |access-date=2022-03-14 |publisher=The Council for the Mathematical Sciences |language=en-GB}}</ref> In 2024 she was elected the first president of the new UK [[Academy for the Mathematical Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/news/acad-math-sci-president-appointed|title=New President of AcadMathSci Announced|publisher=London Mathematical Society|year=2024}}</ref> 

In 2023 she was elected to both the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/new-members-2023|title=New members|year=2023|publisher= American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=2023-04-21}}</ref> and the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2023-nas-election.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230502194908/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2023-nas-election.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=2 May 2023 | title=2023 NAS Election }}</ref>
